title: How Satellite Navigation Works, and NavIC

anim.title: Your phone knows where you are

segments.say: Your phone finds you to within a few metres. It does it by listening to clocks in space.

anim.title: How it works
items: Each satellite broadcasts its time and position
Your phone notes when each signal arrives
Distances from several satellites fix your spot

segments.say: Each satellite keeps broadcasting the exact time and where it is. Your phone sees how late each signal arrives. The delay, times the speed of light, gives the distance.

anim.title: Why four satellites?
anim.below: three for position, one to correct your phone's clock

segments.say: Three distances pin down your position. A fourth fixes the error in your phone's own clock, which is far less precise than the atomic clocks up there.
America has GPS. Russia, Europe and China have their own global systems. India built a regional one: NavIC.
NavIC was designed around seven satellites, high above India. It covers the country and about one thousand five hundred kilometres beyond.

anim.title: Why have our own?
items: Not depending on another country in a crisis
Used in fishing boats, trucks, phones

segments.say: Why bother, when GPS is free? Because another country controls GPS, and can limit it in a crisis. With NavIC, India holds the switch.

anim.title: For your answer
items: Four satellites: 3 for place, 1 for clock

segments.say: For GS Three: navigation is timing; four satellites fix a point; NavIC gives India its own, strategic, signal.

sources: ISRO, NavIC (IRNSS) page: regional navigation system covering India and about 1,500 km beyond its boundary; designed with seven satellites (three geostationary, four geosynchronous); position accuracy better than 20 m
US government, GPS.gov 'How GPS works': receivers use the time signals of at least four satellites to work out position and correct the receiver clock
ISRO, NVS-01 launch (May 2023): second-generation NavIC satellite with an indigenous atomic clock

quiz.q: How does a phone work out its distance to a satellite?
options: From how late the time signal arrives
quiz.why: Delay times the speed of light gives the distance.

quiz.q: Why is a fourth satellite needed?
options: To correct the receiver's clock error
quiz.why: Three fix the position; the fourth corrects the phone's clock.
NavIC covers India and about 1,500 km around it.

reviewNote: Facts were read against ISRO's NavIC page and GPS.gov. Diagrams are schematic, no map. Moving facts: the number of working NavIC satellites changes as old ones fail and new ones launch; the script says 'designed around seven'.
